Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali becomes the first Pakistani to reach orbit and the first foreign national to board China's Tiangong space station, arriving aboard the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft alongside two Chinese astronauts to conduct scientific experiments during a five-day mission.

Jennifer Barreto of Puerto Rico is crowned Miss Universe in San Juan, Puerto Rico, becoming the sixth Puerto-Rican woman, the first mother and married woman to win the title.

items.topic: 2031 and 2035 FIFA Women's World Cup bids
items.text: In association football, FIFA confirms Costa Rica, Jamaica, Mexico, and the United States as joint hosts of the 2031 Women's World Cup, while England, Northern Ireland, Scotland, and Wales will jointly host the 2035 tournament.
The 63rd Golden Horse Awards take place in Taipei, Taiwan, with the Hong Kong film We Are Born Good winning Best Narrative Feature.

The 2026 United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Turkey, concludes without a final agreement after countries failed to reach consensus on fossil fuel policies. It is the longest climate summit on record.
In tennis, Carlos Alcaraz defeats Alexander Zverev 6–2, 7–6 in the final to win his first singles title at the 2026 ATP Finals.

In motorcycle racing, Spanish rider Marc Márquez of Ducati Corse secures his eighth MotoGP World Championship after finishing eighth at the Portuguese Grand Prix, equalling Giacomo Agostini's record for the most premier-class motorcycle racing world titles.

The Japanese trade ministry announces that Saudi Arabia agreed to triple the volume of crude oil stored in Japan to 24 million barrels, under Japan's joint stockpiling system with Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, and the United Arab Emirates.
The European Space Agency announces that the BepiColombo spacecraft inserted itself into orbit around Mercury.
Anthropic employee and mathematician Levent Alpöge releases a claimed proof of the Riemann hypothesis, created with assistance from Claude.

items.topic: AI boom, Initial public offering of Anthropic
items.text: Anthropic holds its initial public offering, raising roughly US$81 billion and becoming the largest IPO in history by amount raised.

The release of American video game Grand Theft Auto VI becomes the biggest launch of an entertainment product in the world with more than $2.3 billion in sales, surpassing the previous record holder, video game Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II (2022), by more than $600 million.

Vincent van Gogh's 1890 painting Blossoming Chestnut Trees sells for US$190.4 million at Sotheby's in New York City, United States, setting a new auction record for Van Gogh and surpassing the $117.2 million paid for Orchard with Cypresses (1888) in 2022.
NASA's space probe Voyager 1 reaches the distance of one light-day from Earth, being the first man-made object to reach that distance, after it launched in 1977.
PlayStation reports a major outage ahead of the release of Grand Theft Auto VI.

items.topic: Bangladeshi cricket team in South Africa in 2026–27
items.text: In Test cricket, Bangladeshi wicketkeeper Litton Das sets a world record for the most dismissals in a single Test innings, recording six catches and two stumpings against South Africa in Johannesburg.

American technology company Apple experiences an outage with several of its services, including Apple Pay, iCloud, the App Store, and AppleCare. The company's spokesperson attributed the problems to an internal update and rules out a cyberattack.
Racing NSW launches an investigation after the body of losing horse So You Are is found in a skip bin in Sydney, Australia.
English actor Robert Pattinson is cast as James Bond in the ongoing film series starring the character.

The European Commission (EC) and the United States Federal Reserve approve Italian bank UniCredit's proposed €45 billion (US$49 billion) acquisition of Germany's Commerzbank, following the European Central Bank's approval in October. The EC grants unconditional antitrust clearance.
Non-profit fanfiction repository website Archive of Our Own is restored to limited functionality 17 days after being targeted in a cyberattack.
In tennis, Kateřina Siniaková and Taylor Townsend win their second and first WTA Finals doubles titles, respectively, after defeating Sara Errani and Jasmine Paolini in the final, 6–4, 6–3.
In tennis, Mirra Andreeva wins her first WTA Finals singles title after defeating Elina Svitolina in the final, 7–5, 6–3.

In golf, Rory McIlroy equals Colin Montgomerie's record for the most Harry Vardon Trophies after winning his eighth Race to Dubai title, which McIlroy claimed after finishing second at the DP World Tour Championship.
In Canadian football, the Edmonton Elks win their 15th Canadian Football League title after beating the Montreal Alouettes 37–30 in the Grey Cup. They previously won in 2015.

items.topic: 2026 Women's Rugby League World Cup, Australia–New Zealand sports rivalries
items.text: In women's rugby league, Australia wins its fourth consecutive World Cup title after defeating New Zealand 34–10 in the final in Brisbane.
In association football, England defeats Spain 3–2 in the group stage of UEFA Nations League A to end Spain's 43-match unbeaten streak, the longest by a national team.
The Philippines wins the inaugural Eurovision Song Contest Asia held in Bangkok, Thailand with the song "Sobra-Sobra" by Carmelle.
A major outage impacts multiple Microsoft services, including Microsoft 365, Copilot and Teams, worldwide.
The Central Bank of Paraguay reports providing partial refunds to 1,812,348 eligible Ueno Bank depositors following the bank's collapse.
The American ocean liner SS United States is sunk off the coast of Destin–Fort Walton Beach, Florida, United States, to become the world's largest artificial reef.

The Thai cabinet approves new environmental regulations for data centers, including limits on noise and temperature increases, requirements for cooling-water recycling and testing, and industrial zoning for facilities consuming more than 20 megawatts.

The United States Food and Drug Administration orders manufacturers of GLP-1 medicines such as semaglutide and tirzepatide, originally intended for the treatment of type 2 diabetes but also commonly used for weight loss, to add warnings that use of such drugs may increase the risk of developing non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, an optic nerve disorder that can cause permanent blindness.
English author M. John Harrison wins the 2026 Booker Prize for his post-apocalyptic novel The End of Everything.

The Pitt Rivers Museum in Oxford, England, United Kingdom, returns the remains of 39 Naga people, collected during the British Raj, to a delegation from Nagaland, India, following six years of discussions over repatriation.

The South Korean Fair Trade Commission issues fines of ₩331.1 billion (US$247 million) for Woowa Brothers and ₩300.8 billion ($222 million) for Coupang, finding that their food-delivery platforms restricted competition by requiring restaurants to match rival platforms' terms.
In college football, the College Football Playoff announces it will expand from 12 to 24 teams starting in the 2027 season.

items.topic: 2026 Formula One World Championship, 2026 São Paulo Grand Prix
items.text: In Formula racing, Mercedes-Benz wins its ninth World Constructors' Championship after drivers George Russell and Kimi Antonelli finished fourth and fifth, respectively, at the São Paulo Grand Prix in Brazil.

In association football, Inter Miami player Lionel Messi is awarded the 2026 Golden Boot Award after scoring 26 goals in one season, becoming the first player in league history to win the award in consecutive years.
In stock car racing, Hendrick Motorsports' driver Kyle Larson wins his third career NASCAR Cup Series championship, becoming the first driver to win two consecutive championships since 2010.

In golf, Blades Brown wins the 2026 World Wide Technology Championship in Los Cabos, Mexico, at 19 years and five months, becoming the youngest PGA Tour winner since 1931 and the fourth-youngest in its history.
In sailing, Frenchman Tom Laperche wins the 2026 Route du Rhum in a record six days, 13 hours, 27 minutes and 40 seconds, beating Charles Caudrelier's 2022 time by six hours and 19 minutes.
